analysis.title: Bitcoin's Next Move
key_insights: BTC has held above its 200-day moving average for 83 days and is tracking toward a 90-day return of 8%. Since 2015, reclaims of the 200-day after a sustained downtrend have shown 180-day forward returns of 53% to 61%, averaging 57%, from a limited sample (attributed to GS).
US spot Bitcoin ETFs had $1.3 billion in outflows last week and another $200 million on Monday. Year-to-date net flows are about negative $1 billion.

Bitcoin miner MARA has sold nearly $1.1 billion of BTC over the past six weeks, per CoinDesk, and plans further sales. The report says institutional demand is weakening as more supply reaches the market.
The number of non-empty Bitcoin wallets has fallen by roughly 109,000 since mid-October, per Santiment, which the report reads as weaker retail participation.
BTC's drop toward $73k set off one of the largest long-liquidation dominance spikes of the past year, at 19%, per Checkonchain. Earlier spikes have often coincided with local lows.
Perpetual futures funding rates fell from about 10% to 5.5% annualized, per CoinMetrics. Funding is still positive, so positioning keeps an upside bias.

tension_points.bull_case: Long-liquidation dominance hit 19%, and earlier spikes often marked local lows. Funding fell from about 10% to 5.5% but is still positive, so positioning keeps an upside bias. BTC is above its 200-day for 83 days, and past reclaims averaged 57% over 180 days.
